title: Expose the existing Autoenvelope (channel) computation via the API
description: IMPORTANT finding: this is NOT a new indicator. `backend/app/indicators/autoenvelope.py` already implements exactly the 'symmetric % channel' concept from Elder ch. 22/41 (EMA(13) +/- rolling average % deviation), fully tested, and already used internally by `app/portfolio/exits.py`'s `evaluate_exit_flags` (the 'price reaches the upper Autoenvelope band with Impulse turning Red' existing-position exit rule from docs/Analyse.md §7). But it's never exposed via any API schema and never drawn on any chart -- confirmed via grep, zero references outside app/portfolio/risk.py, app/signals/impulse.py, app/portfolio/exits.py, app/signals/engine.py. This task is pure exposure: add upper/lower band fields to GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis and the indicator-history endpoint, reusing the existing, already-tested autoenvelope() function -- no new math. This unblocks the frontend channel-overlay task, the profit-target task, and the A-trade-grading task, all of which need channel bounds and currently have no way to get them for an arbitrary ticker (today it's portfolio-position-only, internal).

checklist.step: Confirm autoenvelope()'s existing EMA(13)-based backbone is an acceptable stand-in for the book's own slower-EMA (e.g. 26-day) channel backbone, or decide to add a second, slower-EMA variant -- record as a decisions entry either way (don't silently assume one is fine).
Add upper/lower band fields to the analysis and indicator-history response schemas, sourced from the existing autoenvelope() call, no new computation.
Confirm the exposed values for a portfolio position match what evaluate_exit_flags already computes internally for that same position/date, as a consistency check.
Document the exposure in docs/Analyse.md and docs/architecture/API.md.

decisions.decision: Keep app.indicators.autoenvelope.autoenvelope()'s existing EMA(13) backbone as-is for this exposure -- do not add a second, slower-EMA (e.g. 26-day) channel variant.
decisions.rationale: docs/Analyse.md §4's own indicator table already pins this app's Autoenvelope/Channel row to 'EMA 13 ± avg % deviation' explicitly -- that's this project's own source-of-truth spec, not just a copy of Elder's book, and it was a deliberate choice already recorded on the indicator-autoenvelope task's own `decisions` entry (chosen for consistency with every other daily indicator in this app being EMA(13)-anchored, and because Analyse.md's phrasing doesn't call for a second EMA period). docs/ideas.md's ch. 41 note is correct that Elder's own book prefers a slower EMA (e.g. 26-day) for this specific technique, but this task is scoped as pure exposure -- 'no new math, reusing the existing, already-tested autoenvelope() function' -- and the checklist's own consistency-check item (confirm the exposed values match what evaluate_exit_flags computes internally) only holds cleanly if /analysis and /indicators expose the exact same band evaluate_exit_flags already tests against for the §7 profit-taking exit rule; introducing a second EMA(26) variant here would leave that internal consumer and the newly-exposed API disagreeing on which channel is 'the' channel. Rejected alternative: add a second `channel_upper_26`/`channel_lower_26` (or similar) pair computed via `autoenvelope(close, ema_period=26)` alongside the existing EMA(13) pair -- rejected as new scope/new math this task explicitly excludes, and as duplicating a decision (EMA(13) vs EMA(26) for this indicator) Analyse.md's own table has already made; a future task can revisit this if Analyse.md's own spec changes, but that's a methodology decision, not something to bake into a pure API-exposure task.

decisions.decision: Compute channel_upper/channel_lower inside app.signals.engine.analyse() (added to its indicators dict, alongside ema_13/ema_26/macd_histogram/bull_power/bear_power), not in the router layer -- with optional channel_upper/channel_lower Series passthrough parameters (mirroring the existing ema_13/ema_26/histogram/stochastic_k/force_index_2ema pattern) so analyse_history() can precompute autoenvelope() once over the full daily series and slice it per bar, instead of every one of up to thousands of per-bar analyse() calls independently re-deriving the ~O(n) rolling-deviation-average pass from scratch.
decisions.rationale: Matches this module's existing precompute-and-slice performance pattern (see analyse_history()'s own docstring and docs/tasks/api-stocks-indicator-history-followups.json's `decisions`), which already treats EMA(13)/EMA(26)/MACD-Histogram/Stochastic/Force Index the same way for the identical reason (each is itself O(i) per call, causal/rolling-window, so recomputing over an i-bar-growing slice on every bar is O(range_size x history_length)). autoenvelope()'s rolling(window=100).mean() is the same shape of cost, so leaving it to be recomputed per bar in the naive way would reintroduce exactly the performance problem that prior task already fixed for every other indicator. Rejected alternative: compute the bands in app/api/routers/stocks.py's get_analysis/get_indicator_history handlers directly (calling autoenvelope() there instead of inside analyse()) -- rejected because get_indicator_history doesn't have access to per-bar EMA(13) slices without duplicating analyse_history()'s own precompute machinery, and because every other indicator in AnalysisResponse.indicators is already computed inside analyse() itself, so doing this one differently would be an inconsistent split between the domain (signals) layer and the API layer for no benefit.

decisions.decision: Name the new fields channel_upper/channel_lower (flat, alongside the other Indicators/IndicatorHistoryPoint fields) rather than nesting them under a 'channel' object, and make both nullable (float | None), null whenever the Autoenvelope's ~100-bar deviation-average warm-up window isn't yet full.
decisions.rationale: docs/Analyse.md and docs/architecture/API.md both already call this indicator 'Autoenvelope/channel band' / 'channel line' interchangeably -- 'channel_upper'/'channel_lower' reads naturally against that established vocabulary and against the existing flat-field shape of Indicators/IndicatorHistoryPoint (ema_13, macd_histogram, bull_power, ... -- no nested indicator objects exist in either schema today). Nullability follows the existing precedent set by stochastic_k/force_index_2ema on IndicatorHistoryPoint (both nullable for their own, much shorter warm-up windows) -- but channel_upper/channel_lower need a much longer one (100 bars vs up to 6), so AnalysisResponse.indicators.channel_upper/channel_lower are also nullable (unlike every other AnalysisResponse.indicators field, which is a non-Optional float) since a ticker with under ~100 trading days of history is a real, unremarkable case (not just a theoretical one), not something worth failing the whole request for. Rejected alternative: floor/fall back to a partial-window average (e.g. an expanding-window mean before the rolling window is full) instead of null -- rejected because that would silently produce a statistically meaningless band for a thin history, and because the indicator-autoenvelope task already made and recorded this exact same NaN-not-expanding-average choice for the underlying autoenvelope() function itself; exposing it as null through the API is just carrying that already-made decision through, not making a new one.

comments.summary: Pure additive exposure confirmed: diff touches only app/signals/engine.py (new channel_upper/channel_lower indicators-dict entries + passthrough params, mirroring the existing ema_13/ema_26/histogram/stochastic_k/force_index_2ema precompute-and-slice pattern), the two schemas, the router wiring, docs, and tests. app/signals/confidence.py, app/signals/triple_screen.py, app/signals/impulse.py, app/portfolio/risk.py, and app/portfolio/exits.py's own source are untouched -- no behavior change to Screen 1/2/3, the Impulse gate, confidence scoring, or portfolio risk/exit logic.

Consistency test (TestChannelBandExposureConsistency::test_exposed_channel_bands_match_evaluate_exit_flags_internal_bands) genuinely exercises the claimed guarantee: it spies on app.portfolio.exits.autoenvelope with wraps= (real math, not a stub), captures the actual internal band evaluate_exit_flags computed for a >=100-bar fixture (so the ~100-bar warm-up window is actually full, not trivially NaN==NaN), then asserts analyse() over the same daily/weekly OHLCV reports identical channel_upper/channel_lower. Verified by hand that both call sites share the same EMA(13) formula (ema(daily_close, 13), default autoenvelope() params) so the values are structurally guaranteed to match, not just coincidentally equal on this fixture.

EMA(13)-backbone decision is soundly reasoned and consistent with docs/Analyse.md §4's own indicator table (Row 6: 'EMA 13 ± avg % deviation'), not just Elder's book -- confirmed docs/ideas.md's ch. 41 note (which the decision cites) does describe the book's own preference for a slower EMA, so the decision accurately characterizes that as a different-source preference this app's own spec already overrode, not a mischaracterization.

backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts regenerated correctly: re-ran python scripts/export_openapi.py and yarn generate:api-types locally against this branch and both produced zero diff against what's committed.

Nullability/warm-up handling verified end to end, not just by reading the schema: NaN-to-null conversion through Indicators.channel_upper/channel_lower (float | None, populated from _latest()'s raw NaN, same pattern as the pre-existing stochastic_k/force_index_2ema fields) was confirmed by actually running the relevant integration tests, which assert body['indicators']['channel_upper'] is None during warm-up and a real float after ~100 bars, via response.json() -- not just a type-level check. code-review (high effort) independently investigated this same NaN-serialization path and confirmed FastAPI's response_model path serializes NaN -> null correctly.

Full backend suite: 582 passed, 99.87% overall coverage, engine.py itself at 100% statement/branch coverage. Full frontend suite: 349 passed, 99.69%/99.44%/100%/99.68% (statements/branches/functions/lines). Both well above the 90% gate, no regressions. Backend ruff + mypy clean; frontend eslint + tsc -b clean.

No UI-facing surface in this PR: only frontend/src/api/types.ts changed (a regenerated file), no component/page/hook touched, and no existing frontend code reads the new fields yet (IndicatorsPanel.tsx reads specific named fields only, not a generic iteration that could break). Browser walkthrough (step 9) and the persisted e2e suite (step 9a) were skipped explicitly as not applicable, rather than silently omitted.

Non-blocking: TestAnalyseHistoryPerformance (backend/tests/unit/signals/test_engine.py) has a dedicated wraps=-spy test asserting each of ema/macd_components/stochastic_oscillator/force_index is computed exactly once per analyse_history() call regardless of bar count -- the exact invariant this PR's own second decisions entry extends to autoenvelope() (computed once as channel_bands_full, sliced per bar via .iloc[:i+1]). Manual inspection confirms the code is correct (the call site is outside the per-bar loop), but no analogous spy-based test was added for autoenvelope(), so a future refactor could silently reintroduce a per-bar call without any test catching it. Tracked as backend-channel-envelope-exposure-followups.
